findings.title: Same NPE remains in three getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The PR fixes the NPE in getSubGroupsCount() (line 275) where modelSupplier.get() could return null. However, three other methods on lines 256, 262, and 268 still have the identical vulnerable pattern: `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)`. The Supplier can return null when the underlying group has been deleted concurrently (this is the same race condition that motivated the fix). If a caller invokes any of these overloaded variants while the group is being deleted, an NPE will still be thrown from the auto-unboxing/inner method call. The fix is therefore incomplete and leaves the same crash reachable via subgroup listing code paths.

findings.title: Same NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream(Integer,Integer)
findings.body: Same root cause as the line 256 finding. `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults)` will NPE if modelSupplier.get() returns null, which happens when the group is no longer in the database due to concurrent deletion.

findings.title: Same NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream(String,Boolean,Integer,Integer)
findings.body: Same root cause as the line 256 finding. `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults)` will NPE if modelSupplier.get() returns null under the same concurrent-deletion scenario the PR is trying to fix.

findings.title: Reader thread is not joined before asserting caughtExceptions
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the reader thread is started with `new Thread(() -> {...}).start()` without storing the reference, and the main thread sets `deletedAll.set(true)` and then immediately asserts `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`. There is no `thread.join()` (or CountDownLatch) between flipping the flag and the assertion. If the reader thread is still executing a `groups(...)` call when the assertion runs, any exception it subsequently catches is written to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already been evaluated, causing the test to silently miss failures. This makes the test flaky and unreliable as a regression test for the concurrency bug it is meant to cover.

findings.title: Test does not exercise the actual getSubGroupsCount code path that was fixed
findings.body: The new test createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti only calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` which loads brief representations. The NPE that this PR fixes lives in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(), which is only invoked when the subgroup count is populated (e.g. via GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount, which is only triggered for non-brief representations or when subGroupsCount=true in the admin hierarchy API). As written, the test exercises a different read path and is unlikely to reproduce the original issue 40368, so even if it passes it does not prove the fix is effective.
